# SK1034 — Use the `Count` property, not `Count()` or `Any()`

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

> ⚠ **Retired.** The id stays allocated for ever because every baseline in every repository names it (ADR-012), and the analyzer no longer enables it, so nothing new is reported. This page is here so an old finding can still be looked up.

`list.Count() > 0` and `list.Any()` on something that already has a `Count`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Modernization |
| Status | **retired** — allocated for ever, never reported again |
| Default severity | suggestion (not enabled) |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |

| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 0.6 |

## Why

⚠ **Retired (#281).** `CA1860` and `CA1829` are both enabled by default at `Info` in a stock SDK build and between them report all four of this rule's positive fixtures with nothing configured — `CA1860` three, `CA1829` the `Count()` one — which is the same visibility this rule shipped at (`suggestion`). ADR-008 is host, never rebuild. The id stays allocated for ever (ADR-012). `Enumerable.Count()` has a fast path for `ICollection` and `Any()` allocates an enumerator; both are strictly more work than reading the property, and both hide from the reader that the length is already known. The value is legibility more than speed.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
if (items.Any()) {
    Consume(items);
}
```

Write:

```csharp
if (items.Count > 0) {
    Consume(items);
}
```

## When it does not fire

Only fires when the invoked method is exactly `System.Linq.Enumerable.Count()` or `Enumerable.Any()` with no argument, the receiver's type has an accessible instance `Count` (or `Length`) property of type `int`, and the receiver expression is a plain identifier or member-access chain with no invocation in it — so `GetItems().Any()` is left alone, because reading `.Count` on it would still call `GetItems()` and the rewrite is only obviously equivalent when the receiver is a variable. Silent on `IQueryable`, where `Any()` is a database round-trip and `Count` is not the same query.
